title: Khan Academy regex bypass → 1-click ATO (H1 #3723458)

lab-21-wp-file-inclusion: same family — file inclusion; lab 21 reads local files via traversal, lab 22 executes remote code via include
summary: CVE-2023-3452 (CVSS 9.8): unauthenticated wp_abspath parameter passed into require_once() — data:// wrapper gives single-request RCE when allow_url_include=On. RFI is nearly extinct in modern apps; the misconfiguration is the teaching point.

title: CVE-2023-28131: Expo OAuth proxy open redirect → ATO
related: lab-27-khan-academy-regex-bypass: both are redirect-driven token theft → ATO; Khan bypasses an unescaped-dot regex, Expo bypasses a case-sensitive scheme check
summary: AuthSession proxy (auth.expo.io) stored attacker-influenced returnUrl in an ru cookie, then redirected the OAuth fragment (code+token) to it — the case-sensitive scheme check was bypassed with mixed-case hTTps://. Full ATO demonstrated on Codecademy. CVSS 9.6, hotfixed within hours. Lab: mock OAuth proxy + IdP, no browser needed; fix = case-insensitive scheme + host allowlist (400).

summary: Array-polluting user[email] in the password-reset request redirected the reset link to the attacker's address → one-request ATO with no victim interaction. Critical 10.0, $35,000 bounty verified on the report page.

title: PHP filter chains

summary: CSPT via stylesheet loader — open redirect to CSS injection. HackerOne #1245165 (Acronis); nominated for PortSwigger Top 10 Web Hacking Techniques 2022.

title: Apache 2.4.49 path traversal (CVE-2021-41773)
related: lab-23-gitlab-maven-traversal: same root-cause class — decode-ordering: lab 23 validated the pre-decoded URL, lab 24 checked for .. before decoding %2e to .; lab 23 writes files, lab 24 reads them
lab-21-wp-file-inclusion: same attack family, different root cause — lab 21 is canonicalization without containment, lab 24 is check-then-decode ordering
summary: Disclosed H1 report ($4,000 Internet Bug Bounty on the report page): 2.4.49 checked the path for ../ BEFORE decoding %2e to ., so /.%2e/ segments became live traversal after the check. With ScriptAlias /cgi-bin/ + mod_cgi, a GET reads files outside the web root (e.g. /etc/passwd). Fix is config hardening (Require all denied, per the official advisory); 2.4.50's fix was incomplete (CVE-2021-42013), so the upgrade note says >= 2.4.51.

title: GitLab X-HTTP-Method-Override cache poisoning
summary: Method-override header turns a cacheable GET into an error response that gets cached — cache-poisoned denial of service. $2,500.

title: H1 #1250037: Stripe IDOR email change → ATO
related: finding-gitlab-h1-2293343: both are IDOR → ATO via account identity flows; Stripe changes the account email, GitLab pollutes the reset recipient
lab-28-paypal-idor-privesc: both are IDOR in account management; Stripe takes over accounts via email change, PayPal escalates privilege across merchants
summary: Account-update endpoint not bound to session identity → attacker changed another user's email, then reset the password → full ATO. Critical, $3,000 bounty verified on the report page.

title: HTTP/2: The Sequel is Always Worse

summary: H2.CL downgrade desync — HTTP/2 frontend and HTTP/1 backend disagree on where a request ends, enabling request smuggling.

title: Shopify X-Forwarded-Host cache poisoning
summary: Unkeyed X-Forwarded-Host header poisons cached JS assets — defacement and phishing on apps.shopify.com. Bounty raised from $1,300 to $6,300.

title: Abusing HTTP hop-by-hop request headers
summary: Connection header tricks proxies into stripping security headers (X-Forwarded-For, Authorization) before the backend — enabling admin bypass and IP spoofing.

title: Cache Poisoned Denial of Service (CPDoS)
summary: Caching error responses (e.g. 403s) triggered by attacker-controlled headers — denial of service for every user behind the cache.

title: GitLab Maven registry traversal to authorized_keys write (HackerOne #733072)
related: lab-19-zip-slip: same primitive class — arbitrary file write via traversal; lab 19 via archive entry names, lab 23 via an API file_name segment
lab-21-wp-file-inclusion: same root-cause class — canonicalization without containment; lab 21 reads files, lab 23 writes them
summary: Disclosed H1 report ($1,000 bounty): the Grape router validated the pre-decoded URL, so %2e%2e%2f in the Maven file_name segment passed the no-slash regex — a PUT then wrote the attacker's SSH key over authorized_keys. Traversal on a write sink beats traversal on a read sink.

title: MoPub login open redirect → XSS via javascript: URI (H1 #683298)
related: lab-27-khan-academy-regex-bypass: both are open redirects with real impact; MoPub escalates to XSS via javascript: scheme, Khan steals an auth-transfer token
summary: app.mopub.com/login?next= accepted arbitrary destinations including the javascript: scheme; post-login navigation used window.location.href, so the javascript: URI executed as reflected XSS in the victim's session. Bounty paid (amount not shown on the report page). Lab is the first client-side build, verified with a headless-Chromium sidecar that proves JS execution. Fix: allowlist next to relative paths, reject schemes with 400.

title: PayPal CL.TE desync to stored XSS
related: lab-14-cspt-plugin-xss-ssrf: stored XSS as final impact
summary: CL.TE request smuggling poisons the cache with attacker content — stored XSS on /signin. $18,900.

title: PayPal IDOR → cross-merchant privilege escalation (H1 #415081)
related: finding-stripe-h1-1250037: both are IDOR in account management; PayPal escalates privilege across merchants, Stripe takes over accounts via email change
summary: POST /businessmanage/users/api/v1/users accepted account_id from the request body without checking that the caller is a member of that account — attacker@evil.com added themselves as admin to victim merchant acct_1002, proven by the (properly authorized) read endpoint listing them. High 7.1, $10,500 bounty. Lab: mock merchant API; fix = is_member(email, account_id) before any mutation (cross-merchant → 403).

title: Valve partner CD keys IDOR (H1 #391217)
related: finding-indico-cve-2025-53640: both are missing object authorization → mass exposure; Valve exposes game CD keys, Indico exposes user PII
lab-28-paypal-idor-privesc: both are IDOR/BOLA in partner account flows; Valve leaks mass CD keys, PayPal escalates privilege across merchants
summary: GET /partnercdkeys/assignkeys on partner.steamgames.com performed no object-level authorization → any authenticated partner could download all CD keys of any game. Critical, $20,000 bounty ($15k + bonus). Lab: mock partner portal; exploit pulls 5 real keys of game_5002 as another partner (KEY1 validated against independent oracle); fix = is_owner(email, game_id) → 403.

title: Zip Slip
related: lab-21-wp-file-inclusion: same root-cause class — canonicalization without containment; read vs write primitive
summary: Archive entry names (e.g. ../../pwned.txt) written outside the extraction target — arbitrary file write via crafted archives. Concrete instance: CVE-2018-1002203 in unzipper <0.8.13.

title: Web Cache Deception Attack
related: lab-12-cspt-cache-deception: deception primitive, new vector (CSPT)
